newsitem.title: UK: Shield Diagnostics plans research statement.
newsitem.headline: Shield Diagnostics plans research statement.

text.p: Britain's Shield Diagnostics Group plans to issue a statement on Friday clarifying the progress of its product research, the Financial Times reported.
Shield's leading product is a heart disease diagnostic, a test for a chemical called AFT in the blood. It is seen as a method of diagnosing vulnerability to heart attacks.
Current research in Britain and the United States is attempting to clarify whether there is a link between AFT and heart disease.
Although the results are not due until June, the Financial Times said Shield hoped to reveal whether or not there had been significant progress in the research.
Rumours that the company may be close to discovering a new test for heart disease have fuelled a sharp rise in the company's share price over the last month.
The Financial Times valued the potential market for the test at around 500 million pounds ($808.5 million) a year. ($1=.6184 Pound)
